shortDescription: India's Jindal Stainless NSE:JSL reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports.Here are some key details:($1 = 94.8800 Indian rupees)

children: reported an 11.1% rise in second-quarter profit on Thursday, led by strong sales volume growth, especially in exports.
Consolidated net profit for India's biggest stainless-steel producer rose to 8.98 billion rupees ($94.7 million) in the quarter ended September 30 from 8.08 billion rupees a year ago
Analysts, on average, had expected a profit of 8.36 billion rupees, according to data compiled by LSEG
Higher volumes and resilient stainless steel demand were expected to boost second-quarter earnings, according to analysts at ICICI Securities
Sales volume rose 2.5% year-on-year to 664,378 tons, led by a 36% jump in exports
Domestic sales comprised 89% of total sales, down from 91% a year ago, while exports were 11% of total sales during the quarter
Revenue rose 18.2% to 128.74 billion rupees; EBITDA grew 3.2% year-on-year to 14.33 billion rupees

The quarter marked a resilient recovery following the operational disruptions in the previous three months, which had been impacted by the geopolitical situation and industrial gas availability constraints - Jindal Stainless
The company also flagged increased import pressure, especially from China
"The first four months of FY27 alone account for about 63% of the entire previous year's imports from China," the stainless steel maker said
Jindal Stainless operates 16 stainless-steel facilities across India, Spain and Indonesia, with a network spanning 12 countries
